findings.title: Concurrent index init has data races on counter and error
findings.body: In searchSupport.init each errgroup worker runs `totalBatchesIndexed++` and `_, _, err = s.build(...)` where both variables are shared across workers without synchronization. Concurrent increments lose counts and concurrent assignments to the outer err race, so one worker can overwrite another's error before it is returned and the race detector will flag it. Use a local err variable inside the closure and an atomic counter.

findings.title: TotalDocs reads cache map without lock
findings.body: bleveBackend.TotalDocs iterates `b.cache` with no lock while BuildIndex writes `b.cache[key] = idx` under cacheMu and GetIndex reads under RLock. Concurrent map read and write is a data race that can panic at runtime. The PR makes concurrent builds expected, and the search watch goroutine can trigger builds concurrent with the TotalDocs call in init.

findings.title: Removing global BuildIndex lock allows duplicate builds for same key
findings.body: BuildIndex previously held cacheMu for the whole build; now it only locks for the final map insert. Two concurrent getOrCreateIndex calls for the same NamespacedResource can both see GetIndex return nil, both build separate bleve indexes, and last-writer-wins. This wastes work, double-increments IndexTenants metrics, leaks the loser's index, and for file-backed indexes both call bleve.New on the same directory so one fails.

findings.title: Search watch loop uses uncanceled Background context and ignores close
findings.body: searchSupport.init creates watchctx as context.Background with no cancel and loops `for { v := <-events; handleEvent(watchctx, v) }` without checking channel closure. The goroutine never exits on server Stop, leaking forever, and when the backend closes the channel the loop spins on zero values and handleEvent dereferences a nil event and panics.

findings.title: Broadcaster pipe ignores channel close and cancellation
findings.body: server.initWatcher starts a goroutine doing `v := <-events` without checking ok, then logs v.Type, stores v.ResourceVersion and blocks on `out <- v` with no select on context. When the storage backend closes the stream the loop receives nil forever and panics on dereference, and if the broadcaster stops the send blocks forever and leaks the goroutine.

findings.title: Eager Init leaks cancel and blocks startup with no timeout
findings.body: NewResourceServer creates a cancelable server context then calls s.Init synchronously. On Init failure it returns nil and error without calling cancel, leaking the context. More broadly the long synchronous search-index build now blocks module startup; transient DB or index errors that previously surfaced on first RPC now prevent the whole server from being constructed.

findings.title: History and Origin panic when search is disabled
findings.body: When Search.Resources is nil, s.search stays nil. server.Search checks for nil and returns an error, but server.History and server.Origin directly call s.search.History and s.search.Origin with no guard, causing a nil pointer dereference panic instead of an error.

findings.title: Trace context still discarded on write path
findings.body: WriteEvent and create/update/delete still do `_, span := tracer.Start` and pass the original context to children, so child spans become siblings of the parent instead of children. Only GetResourceStats was fixed to `ctx, span`, leaving the main write and read trace hierarchy broken despite the PR claiming to fix propagation.

findings.title: Skipping postgres integration test hides regressions
findings.body: The change adds a skip for the storage-server instrumentation test when GRAFANA_TEST_DB is postgres with only a TODO. Unified storage behavior is dialect dependent, so skipping removes coverage for the exact startup and init path this PR changes without a linked issue or alternative coverage.
